name: Protective Put Spread
aliases: Hedged with a bear put spread
summary: Hedge shares with a long put financed partly by a lower short put, cutting hedge cost at the price of protection below the short strike.

legs.dte_rule: same expiry as the long put

max_loss: (share basis - long strike + net debit) x 100 PLUS unlimited further loss below the short strike - protection stops there
breakevens: share basis + net debit per share
when_to_use: When a plain protective put is too expensive (IV Rank >= 50) and the system wants protection over a defined band - typically a 5-15% decline - while accepting that a crash below the short strike is unhedged.
entry_rules: Net debit <= 1.2% of share notional per 90-day hedge.
Long strike by delta in [0.30, 0.40]; short strike by delta in [0.12, 0.18]; width >= 7% of spot.
Require cash or margin to support the short put if it is assigned (it is covered only by the long put for margin, but assignment delivers shares).
Require IV skew to favor the structure: short put IV - long put IV >= 2 vol points.
Both legs same expiry; OI >= 250 each.
management_rules: Close the whole spread when the long put's delta exceeds 0.70 (the hedge has done its job) and re-strike lower if protection is still needed.
If the stock rallies and the spread decays to <= 20% of the debit, close it and re-hedge higher.
exit_rules: HARD: the SHORT put is the assignable leg. Close it by 15:30 ET on expiration day if ITM, and any time its extrinsic < 0.05 and delta < -0.85. Assignment delivers 100 MORE shares, doubling the long exposure at the worst moment.
Close the long put rather than letting it auto-exercise into a share sale.
Close both legs together as one combo order.
assignment_risk: The short put is assignable and, if assigned, converts a hedge into a doubled share position at the short strike while the long put remains. This is the key hazard: a hedge that becomes leverage. Monitor extrinsic continuously.
buying_power: Net debit; the spread is defined risk for margin purposes (long put covers the short put), so level 3 is sufficient.
liquidity_needs: Two strikes with OI >= 250 each; combined spread <= 12% of net debit.
common_mistakes: Believing the position is fully hedged; the cheapest configurations leave the tail completely open. Forgetting that short put assignment adds shares.
zero_dte_notes: Not applicable as a hedge structure.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
